verses.1: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.2: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
verses.3: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
verses.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
verses.5: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
verses.6:
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared:
 “I am young in years,
 while you are old;
 that is why I was timid and afraid
 to tell you what I know.
verses.7:
I thought that age should speak,
 and many years should teach wisdom.
verses.8:
But there is a spirit + 32:8 Or the Spirit ; similarly in verse 18 in a man,
 the breath of the Almighty,
 that gives him understanding.
verses.9:
It is not only the old + 32:9 Or many or great who are wise,
 or the elderly who understand justice.
verses.10:
Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me;
 I too will declare what I know.’
verses.13:
So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom;
 let God, not man, refute him.’
verses.14:
But Job has not directed his words against me,
 and I will not answer him with your arguments.
verses.15:
Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say;
 words have escaped them.
verses.16:
Must I wait, now that they are silent,
 now that they stand and no longer reply?
verses.17:
I too will answer;
 yes, I will declare what I know.
verses.18:
For I am full of words,
 and my spirit within me compels me.
verses.19:
Behold, my belly is like unvented wine;
 it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
verses.20:
I must speak and find relief;
 I must open my lips and respond.
verses.21:
I will be partial to no one,
 nor will I flatter any man.
verses.22:
For I do not know how to flatter,
 or my Maker would remove me in an instant.[’’]
